contents.name: 13.1 conductor charge relaxation and the telegraph equation (13.1)-(13.4): j=sigma E, exponential charge decay, the damped wave equation
contents.reason: The Ohmic conductor branch (charge relaxation, complex wave number, skin effect) is built on the wave-interfaces pair of batch 34, which owns the finite-conductivity and skin-depth items; this pair treats only the ideal PEC boundary model of the lossless guide and derives no Ohmic material behaviour.

contents.name: 13.1 spatially decaying wave and skin effect: k=(k_r+i k_i)e_z, k_i=mu sigma omega/(2k_r), field penetration depth 1/k_i (13.7)-(13.9)
contents.reason: The penetration depth and the selection of the complex root belong to the Ohmic constitutive branch on the wave-interfaces pair; no claim of this pair depends on them, and the sigma=0 lossless branch used here is the no-attenuation specialization.

contents.name: 13.2 guide setup and phasor reduction (13.10)-(13.13): cylindrical hollow conductor along z, transverse region A, F=Re[F(x,y)e^{ikz}e^{-i omega t}], two-dimensional vector/scalar split
contents.support: The definition fixes the straight guide region, the axis, the transverse decomposition and the beta-omega separated phasor convention e^{i(beta x3-omega t)}; the calculus of the real parts is isolated in [[lem-em-separated-phasor-calculus]].

contents.name: 13.2 transverse algebra and the duality operation (13.14)-(13.16): F^x=F x e_z identities, the split cross product and the split of the three-dimensional curl
contents.support: The lemma proves the identities e_z x (e_z x grad_t h)=-grad_t h, div(e_z x grad_t h)=0, curl(e_z x grad_t h)=e_z Delta_t h and the transverse curl/divergence formulas used throughout the reduction.

contents.name: 13.2 three-dimensional wave equation reduced to the transverse eigenvalue equation Delta Psi=-lambda Psi with lambda=omega^2/c^2-k^2 (13.17)-(13.18)
contents.support: The medium version Delta_t F=-k_c^2 F with k_c^2=omega^2 epsilon mu-beta^2 is proved for the explicit profiles in the candidate theorem and the profile lemma; the vacuum relation is the specialization epsilon mu=c^{-2}.

contents.name: 13.2 source-free Maxwell split and reduction to the transverse electric field (13.19)-(13.21), with e,b determined by E and overdetermined equations reducing to the wave equation
contents.support: The candidate theorem verifies the four source-free macroscopic phasor equations directly for the TE and TM families, with div E=div H=0 and the two curl equations; no hidden overdetermined system is assumed.

contents.name: 13.2 PEC boundary conditions (13.22)-(13.23): n x E3=0 and n.B3=0 on the boundary, equivalently e=0, n.E^x=0, n.B=0
contents.support: The definition declares n x E=0 and n.B=0 on the open walls as the ideal PEC boundary model, with its interface reading from [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] and the explicit exclusion of the box edges and of the sigma to infinity limit.

contents.name: 13.2 guide eigenvalue problem and dispersion omega=c sqrt(lambda_n+k^2), k=sqrt(omega^2/c^2-lambda_n) (13.24)-(13.25)
contents.support: The dispersion relation beta^2=omega^2 epsilon mu-k_c^2, the cutoff omega_c=k_c/sqrt(epsilon mu) and the phase/group speeds of the branch are stated and proved in the dispersion-energy theorem.

contents.name: 13.2 spectrum positivity from the Green identity (13.26)-(13.27)
contents.reason: Positivity and reality of the transverse spectrum is the mathematical spectral closure supplied by the boundary-and-spectral prerequisites page (items thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness and lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure); the source's printed identity (13.26) also omits a conjugate Re(E*.Delta E), which the run recorded as a source defect and does not copy.

contents.name: 13.2 propagating versus evanescent modes at fixed omega and the finiteness of the propagating set (13.28)
contents.support: Clauses (c) and (d) of the dispersion-energy theorem give the propagating branch and the explicit index bounds m<omega a sqrt(epsilon mu)/pi, n<omega b sqrt(epsilon mu)/pi that confine the propagating indices.

contents.name: 13.2 TE and TM scalar reductions (13.29)-(13.32): E from grad e and e_z x grad b, e=0 (Dirichlet) and n.grad b=0 (Neumann)
contents.support: The theorem's TE family uses the Neumann profile h and the TM family the Dirichlet profile e with exactly these boundary traces; the explicit phasors record the tangent/rotated-gradient relations.

contents.name: 13.2 TEM case lambda=0 (13.33)-(13.35): harmonic transverse fields, simply connected cross section gives Phi=const and E=0, one TEM mode per hole for multiply connected compact cross sections
contents.support: The example proves the harmonic-potential form, the single-conductor obstruction via two-dimensional Dirichlet uniqueness, and exhibits the coaxial annulus with its two boundary components carrying distinct constants.

contents.name: 13.2 rectangular hollow guide modes: TE(n_x,n_y) cos cos (not both zero), TM(n_x,n_y) sin sin (both positive), eigenvalues lambda=pi^2(n_x^2/d_x^2+n_y^2/d_y^2) (13.36)-(13.37)
contents.support: The candidate theorem states and verifies exactly these index families, their index restrictions and the eigenvalue identity of the profiles.

contents.name: 13.2 plane-wave superposition interpretation of the guide modes (13.39) and the circular guide with Bessel functions (13.40)-(13.42)
contents.reason: The plane-wave-reflection picture is an interpretive reading not needed by the scaffolded proofs, and the circular-cross-section Bessel guide lies outside this rectangular pair's declared geometry; the source's TE 'Wendepunkt' label is also a recorded defect, so nothing is built on it.

contents.name: 13.2 energy per length and flux of a guide mode (13.43)-(13.44) and the identification of their ratio with the group velocity c^2 k/omega (13.45)
contents.support: The theorem's clauses (b) and (c) give the period-averaged cross-section energy U, flux Phi and the exact identity Phi/U=beta/(epsilon mu omega)=d omega/d beta, with the medium stored-energy density of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]].

contents.name: 13.3 cavities: three-dimensional eigenvalue problem Delta Psi=-lambda Psi, discrete geometry-dependent spectrum (13.46)-(13.47)
contents.support: Clause (c) states the smooth PEC cavity curl eigenbasis with discrete nonnegative eigenvalues of finite multiplicity and retention of the zero modes, and clause (b) the rectangular reflection class.

contents.name: 13.3 terminated waveguide cavity A x [0,d_z]: standing waves k_z=+/-pi n_z/d_z, TE b(z)~sin(pi n_z z/d_z), TM e(z)~cos(pi n_z z/d_z), spectrum omega=c sqrt(lambda+pi^2 n_z^2/d_z^2) (13.48)-(13.50)
contents.support: The example is the explicit TM (1,1,1)-type standing mode of the box with resonance omega^2=(epsilon mu)^{-1}[(pi/b)^2+(pi/d)^2] and the full end-cap check; the general separated Fourier modes of the reflection class are clause (b) of the completeness theorem.

contents.name: Rectangular guide TE_mn modes B_z=B_0 cos(k_x x)cos(k_y y), index quantisation, dispersion k^2 c^2=omega^2-omega_mn^2, cutoff omega_mn and lowest TE_10 cutoff (1304)-(1309)

contents.name: Phase velocity omega/k>c and group velocity d omega/d k<c for the TE_mn branch, with energy transmitted at the group velocity (1310)-(1311)
contents.support: Clauses (c)-(d) give v_p=omega/beta, v_g=beta/(epsilon mu omega), v_p v_g=1/(epsilon mu), 0<v_g<1/sqrt(epsilon mu) and Phi/U=v_g for the declared propagating branch.

contents.name: TM_mn modes E_z=E_0 sin(k_x x)sin(k_y y), Dirichlet quantisation n,m>=1, TM_11 lowest TM cutoff, lowest mode always TE (1312)-(1315)

contents.name: TEM modes: omega^2=k^2c^2, E_t=-grad phi, B_t=c^{-1} grad phi x e_z, Laplacian equation for phi, phi constant on the walls, no nontrivial TEM in a conventional waveguide (1316)-(1320)
contents.support: The example's potential-form reduction proves the field relations and the boundary equation, and the single-conductor obstruction proves the nonexistence clause for connected boundary; the vacuum c is the medium v=(epsilon mu)^{-1/2} specialization.

contents.name: Coaxial guide solution phi=phi_b ln(r/b), inner conductor required, no cutoff frequency and phase=group velocity c (1321)-(1322) and the transmission-line reading
contents.support: The coaxial clause exhibits phi=V ln(b/|x|)/ln(b/a), the radial field, the PEC conditions, k=omega/v with no cutoff and the exact per-length energies W_e=W_m=CV^2/2 with LC=epsilon mu.

sources.title: D. J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 3rd edition (Prentice Hall 1999, 596-page retained scan)
sources.locator: Section 9.5 'Guided Waves' printed pp. 405-412: 9.5.1 wave guides pp. 405-408 with Problems 9.26-9.27; 9.5.2 TE waves in a rectangular wave guide pp. 408-411 with Problems 9.28-9.30; 9.5.3 the coaxial transmission line pp. 411-412 with Problem 9.31. Read in the stamped 596-page full scan; OCR noise in the text layer was cross-checked against the other two treatments.

contents.name: 9.5.1 wave guides: perfect-conductor assumptions E=B=0 inside, boundary conditions E_parallel=0 and B_perp=0, induced surface charges and currents (9.175 with footnote 16)
contents.support: The definition's PEC clause states n x E=0 and n.B=0 with the surface-charge and surface-current readings n.D=sigma_f and n x H=K_f determined by the traces; the perfect-conductor limit is declared as an idealization.

contents.name: 9.5.1 monochromatic guide ansatz E(x,y)e^{i(kz-omega t)}, longitudinal decomposition E=E_x x+E_y y+E_z z, the six algebraic Maxwell relations (9.176)-(9.179)
contents.support: The theorem works in the separated phasor convention of the definition and verifies the four source-free phasor equations for the TE and TM families; the six relations are the component forms of those equations.

contents.name: 9.5.1 solution for the transverse components and uncoupled equations for E_z, B_z; definitions TE (E_z=0), TM (B_z=0), TEM (both) (9.180)-(9.181)
contents.support: The definition fixes the TE/TM/TEM terminology relative to the named axis and the theorem states the explicit separated families; the second-derivative profile identities are the profile lemma.

contents.name: 9.5.1 hollow wave guides cannot support TEM waves: the transverse E field is divergence- and curl-free, hence a Laplace-equation gradient with constant boundary value, hence zero (pp. 407-408)
contents.support: The example proves the potential-form reduction, the constancy of the potential on each boundary component and the vanishing on a single-conductor cross-section by two-dimensional Dirichlet uniqueness; it also exhibits the coaxial counterexample.

contents.name: 9.5.2 TE_mn rectangular modes: separation, quantised k_x=m pi/a, k_y=n pi/b, at least one index nonzero, B_z=B_0 cos cos, k=sqrt((omega/c)^2-pi^2[(m/a)^2+(n/b)^2]) and cutoff (9.182)-(9.190)
contents.support: The theorem proves the general TE family and index exclusions; the TE10 example records the explicit amplitudes, the half-sine standing profile, the cutoff and the lowest-cutoff comparison.

contents.name: 9.5.2 phase velocity c/sqrt(1-(omega_mn/omega)^2)>c and energy transport at the group velocity c sqrt(1-(omega_mn/omega)^2)<c, with the plane-wave reflection picture (9.191)-(9.192, Fig. 9.25)
contents.support: The theorem's clauses (c)-(d) prove the exact medium identities v_p=omega/beta, v_g=beta/(epsilon mu omega) and Phi/U=v_g; the reflection picture itself is not used.

contents.name: Problem 9.27 TE_00 cannot occur (indeterminate case leading back to TEM)
contents.support: Clause (c) excludes (m,n)=(0,0) by the divergence equation; the excluded case is exactly the source's TE_00.

contents.name: Problem 9.29 confirmation that the TE_mn energy travels at the group velocity (time-averaged Poynting flux over cross section divided by energy per length)
contents.support: The theorem proves the period-averaged cross-section flux and energy with the ratio beta/(epsilon mu omega); the computation is carried out here rather than taken from the problem hint.

contents.name: Problem 9.30 theory of TM modes: longitudinal field, cutoff frequencies, wave and group velocities, lowest TM cutoff relative to the lowest TE cutoff
contents.support: The TM family with m,n>=1, its cutoff k_c=sqrt((m pi/a)^2+(n pi/b)^2) and the index restrictions are proved in the theorem; the comparison is the cutoff clause.

contents.name: 9.5.3 coaxial transmission line: TEM branch with k=omega/c, cB_y=E_x, cB_x=-E_y, the two-dimensional electrostatic/magnetostatic problem, E_s=A e_s/s and B_phi=A e_phi/(c s), the real fields (9.193)-(9.197)
contents.support: The coaxial clause gives E_t=-grad phi with phi=V ln(b/|x|)/ln(b/a), H_t=Z^{-1}e_z x E_t, k=omega/v, the PEC conditions and the per-length capacitance and inductance; the source's vacuum c is instantiated at v.

contents.name: Problem 9.31 direct verification of the coaxial fields and the surface charge and current on the inner conductor
contents.support: The example proves the field equations in the potential form and the PEC conditions; the surface readings are declared as determined by the interface supplier rather than computed here.

contents.name: More Problems on Chapter 9: Fourier inversion, spherical wave, rectangular cavity and dielectric waveguide exercises (9.32-9.41 region)
contents.reason: These are exercises on Fourier inversion, spherical waves, rectangular-cavity mode counting, dielectric slab and fiber guides, and wave-guide dispersion exercises; none is a source-backed result promised by this pair's design and several lie outside the declared rectangular lossless geometry.
